annotationRationale: Reflection properties establish area preservation, while coordinate signs and slopes verify the other claims and provide a parallel-side counterexample.
sourceMethod: Followed the official reflection-properties solution and its counterexample with AB parallel to y = x; supplied explicit vertices and slope calculations.

review.mathCheck: Coordinate swapping preserves positive coordinates and reflection preserves area. Since each vertex is off y=x, the connecting slope is (a−b)/(b−a)=−1, establishing C and D. The proposed three vertices are positive, off the axis, and noncollinear. AB is y=x+1 and A′B′ is y=x−1, so these distinct parallel lines disprove E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of numbered MAA solution 5. It retains coordinate swapping, area preservation, and the side-parallel-to-y=x counterexample, adding explicit coordinates and slope calculations. No general classification of reflected slopes is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Reflection properties are appropriately assessed. Quadrant signs, the two-point slope formula, and slope-based parallelism are all used supporting concepts. The off-axis condition correctly prevents zero denominators.
